notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c) at head 3e3581d, uncommitted false: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, 29 skills listed. No transcript has a Skill tool call or any SKILL.md text (zgrep for 'Readability rules carry the same weight' finds nothing; the Skill name appears only in the tool list), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires. In the scratch folder, mix format --check-formatted passes for opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 and fails for haiku-2 (line 22, a 103-character @spec) and sonnet-1 (line 29, 100 characters), matching format_ok; all five compile with --warnings-as-errors against a Decimal stand-in. A probe with that stand-in gives the expected per-currency totals, most recent order of any status and top-5 order for all five. A second probe with a completed row missing "amount" shows opus-1 returning {:error, {:invalid_order, ...}}, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 raising, and sonnet-1 silently leaving the row out of totals and the completed count. Haiku-2 left check/ (a float-based Decimal stand-in, run.exs and .beam files) in its run folder from its own smoke test; it is not graded.

git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes one rule in this case's list, "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else". Its other changes are outside the list: the How to use this skill bullets, a defstruct sentence in Update structs, two new rules (Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call; Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order), Before you finish step 4, an example under Use ETS for data many processes read in processes.md (the text of Decide whether you need a process is unchanged), and testing.md. The other nine rules are graded to the standard of the 2026-10-22-b grade files: the per-key fold row of the Enum/Map table, with Decimal sums by Enum.reduce over a group as reductions no row replaces; a literal map plus Map.fetch counted as explicit clauses; an unreversed prepend that nothing orders by held clean; acc, id, string and value passing Naming while single letters fail; and the same catch-all, raise, boundary-parsing, @doc, nesting, pipeline and format listings outside the list. Neither new rule finds a violation: no module has use, import, alias or require, and no multi-line map or keyword list is passed straight to a call.

Changed rule, graded per sentence against the current text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else". The sentences that decide it now are "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper." and "The same holds for `if`: `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` fits when each branch is one short expression on the `if`'s line, and a branch `mix format` moves onto its own line gets `do ... end`." No run has a do: body on a function or an if that mix format wrapped onto its own line, as written or after formatting a copy (the formatter changes only haiku-2 line 22, a @spec, and sonnet-1 line 29, a map field), so there is nothing to quote for those sentences; the guard-wrap exception is not used. Every do: in the five files is on its head's line: opus-1 lines 119, 128 and 147; haiku-1 lines 68, 69 and 86 (an if); haiku-2 lines 92-93; sonnet-1 lines 57 and 59 (an if inside a do:); sonnet-2 has none. Violating runs out of 5, per sentence: one-expression do: 0; several steps, case, with or comment under do: 0; block clause among do: clauses without a blank line 0 (opus-1 parse/1, parse_amount/1 and parse_datetime/1, sonnet-1 add_completed/2, each with one block clause of two, set apart); most clauses blocks but some do: 0; do: body wrapped onto its own line 0; if branch wrapped onto its own line 0. The previous sweep's judgement calls do not recur: sonnet-1's defp latest(a, b), do: if(...) (line 59) is now decided by the if sentence and is clean, its branches being one short expression each on one line; haiku-1's if at line 86 is one line too. No run writes the wrapped if the previous sweep held fine in its haiku-1 (lines 79-81), which the new sentence would now count as violated.

Against the previous sweep's baseline: the with rule is violated again in opus-1 (a one-step with in build/1, lines 48-50, the shape the 2026-10-22 sweep flagged in its opus-1); the other four raise on bad input and write no with. Enum/Map is violated in opus-1 (a per-currency for reduce: with Map.update), sonnet-1 (whole per-customer fold with Map.update and a hand-kept count) and sonnet-2 (per-currency for reduce:), and clean in both Haiku runs, which use group_by/3 with Map.new per currency (haiku-1 with integer cents and Enum.sum, haiku-2 with an Enum.reduce over Decimal.add/2), the reverse of the previous sweep's tiers. Naming is violated only by sonnet-1 (latest(a, b) again, plus c and n). The captures rule is violated by sonnet-1 line 54, the two-call capture wrapping an fn that the 2026-10-22 sweep flagged in its sonnet-2. Outside the list: a Decimal.parse/1 catch-all in opus-1; a case in a case (opus-1) and an if in an if (haiku-1); raising on malformed rows in haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; string-keyed rows read or parsed inside the report code in haiku-1 and sonnet-1; sonnet-1's add_completed/2 head that selects and matches fields at once; two pipeline steps on one line in haiku-1 and sonnet-1; a @doc without ## Examples in opus-1 and sonnet-2 and no @doc in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1; mix format failures in haiku-2 and sonnet-1.
